title: Flat-prime support argument and smooth composition
statement: Let $R$ be a Noetherian commutative ring [def-weil-pbc-noetherian-ring], $D$ a finitely presented $R$-algebra [def-weil-pbc-finitely-presented-algebra], $B$ a commutative $R$-algebra, and $d_B:D\to B$ an $R$-algebra map making $B$ finitely presented over $D$. Let $\pi\in R$ satisfy $\operatorname{Ann}_R(\pi)=\operatorname{Ann}_R(\pi^2)$. Write $p$ for its image in $D$, and $T=\{r\in D\mid\forall x\in D,\ p^2x=0\Rightarrow rpx=0\}$. If the ideal generated by $d_B(T)$ is contained in $H_{B/D}$, then $H_{D/R}B\subset H_{B/D}$ and $H_{D/R}B\subset H_{B/R}$, with $H$ the singular ideals [def-weil-pbc-singular-ideal] and the $D$-algebra structure on $B$ induced by $d_B$.

source.place: Stacks Tag 07CT, proof: Flat-prime support argument and smooth composition

proof.text: Claim: if $\mathfrak q\subset D$ is a prime such that $D_{\mathfrak q}$ is flat over $R$, then $\mathfrak a\not\subset\mathfrak q$. Proof. For $k=1,2$, [lem-weil-pbc-annihilator-element-flat-base-change] applied to the flat map $R\to D_{\mathfrak q}$ and $x=\pi^k$ gives $\mathrm{Ann}_{D_{\mathfrak q}}(\pi^k)=\mathrm{Ann}_R(\pi^k)D_{\mathfrak q}$; since $\mathrm{Ann}_R(\pi)=\mathrm{Ann}_R(\pi^2)$ we get $\mathrm{Ann}_{D_{\mathfrak q}}(\pi^2)=\mathrm{Ann}_{D_{\mathfrak q}}(\pi)$. Hence $M_{\mathfrak q}=0$: for $x\in\mathrm{Ann}_D(\pi_D^2)$ the element $x/1\in D_{\mathfrak q}$ is killed by $\pi^2$, hence by $\pi$, so $\pi x/1=0$ and there is $s\in D\setminus\mathfrak q$ with $s\pi_Dx=0$, i.e. $sx\in\mathrm{Ann}_D(\pi_D)$ and the class of $x$ in $M$ maps to $0$ in $M_{\mathfrak q}$. The $D$-module $M$ is finitely generated, being a quotient of the ideal $\mathrm{Ann}_D(\pi_D^2)$ of the Noetherian ring $D$ (finite type over the Noetherian base). By [lem-weil-pbc-finite-module-support-annihilator], $M_{\mathfrak q}=0$ gives $\mathfrak a=\mathrm{Ann}_D(M)\not\subset\mathfrak q$.

source.place: Smoothing Ring Maps, proof of Lemma Tag 07CT (lemma-desingularize-strictly-standard, lines 1831-1860), fifth to seventh sentences ('For any prime q of D such that D_q is flat over R we have Ann_{D_q}(pi^2)/Ann_{D_q}(pi) = 0 because annihilators of elements commutes with flat base change [Algebra 07T8] ... Because D is Noetherian ... formation of its annihilator commutes with localization. Thus we see that a is not contained in q')

proof.text: If $R\to D$ is smooth at a prime $\mathfrak q\subset D$ (in the sense of [def-weil-pbc-singular-ideal]), then $D_{\mathfrak q}$ is flat over $R$: choose $g\in D\setminus\mathfrak q$ with $D_g$ smooth over $R$; then $R\to D_g$ is flat [lem-weil-pbc-smooth-ring-map-flat]; $D_{\mathfrak q}$ is the localization of $D_g$ at the prime $\mathfrak qD_g$ (the elements of $D\setminus\mathfrak q$ and $g$ are units in $D_{\mathfrak q}$, and the universal properties of localization identify the two rings), so $D_g\to D_{\mathfrak q}$ is flat [lem-weil-pbc-localization-flat]; and the composite $R\to D_g\to D_{\mathfrak q}$ is flat [lem-weil-pbc-flat-ring-map-comp].
